History:
- Main complaint: Reduced hearing in the left ear with intermittent ringing (tinnitus) for ~6 weeks.
- Course: Intermittent; prior brief episode about 1 year ago lasting a couple of days.
- Laterality: Left ear only; right ear perceived as normal.
- Associated symptoms: Intermittent dizziness described as feeling off-balance; denies room-spinning vertigo. Chest pain denied. Fever denied.
- Ear-specific symptoms: No ear pain. No ear discharge. Itchiness not documented.
- Triggers/timing: Patient stated some activities affect ringing; mentioned watching TV/listening to music, described as “triggers” but also said it “solves” the ringing (conflict noted).
- Self-care/Exposures: Does not use cotton buds.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic conditions: Not documented.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications: Not documented.
- Prior hospitalizations/surgeries: Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- No in-person exam performed during this video visit; otoscopic exam pending.
- No vital signs recorded.

Impression:
- Left-sided hearing loss with tinnitus and intermittent non-vertiginous dizziness; need to rule out conductive cause such as cerumen impaction vs other middle/inner ear pathology.

Management Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face clinic visit within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to assess for wax/physical blockage and evaluate the tympanic membrane.
- Provide patient education: Link to tinnitus information leaflet placed in visit notes for review before in-person appointment.
- Scheduling: Patient to call support team to book the in-person slot as advised.
- Safety/contingency: If any issues arise before the clinic visit, patient to book another video appointment.

Patient Summary:
- Adult male with 6 weeks of intermittent left-sided hearing reduction and tinnitus, with occasional non-spinning dizziness. No pain, discharge, or fever. Plan is to perform in-person ear exam to rule out wax or other ear pathology and guide next steps; tinnitus education provided.

Key Takeaways:
- Attend in-person ear exam within 4–5 days to check for blockage or other ear findings.
- Review the tinnitus information provided to understand symptoms and management options.
- Avoid using cotton buds; seek follow-up if symptoms worsen before the appointment.

Next Steps:
- In-person otoscopic exam.
- Subsequent management to be determined based on exam findings and discussion at follow-up.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Allergies, current medication list, full past medical/surgical history, vitals, detailed ROS (palpitations response not documented; ear itchiness not answered), noise/ototoxic exposure history not obtained.
- Internal conflicts: 
  • Tinnitus modulation described as both “triggered” and “solved” by TV/music. 
  • Nausea: initially implied feeling “a bit sick,” later stated dizziness not associated with nausea. 
  • Name discrepancy: patient stated “Jack Smith,” clinician addressed as “John.”
- Transcript quality: Some pauses/inaudible segments and overlapping speech leading to minor ambiguities.
